exposure: Timing of pregnancy (mid pregnancy vs. late pregnancy)
outcome: Prevalence of fear of birth (FOBS score >=60)
cohort: The study included a one-year cohort of 1212 pregnant women from a northern part of Sweden, recruited in mid pregnancy and followed up in late pregnancy.
finding: The prevalence of fear of birth decreased significantly from 22% in mid-pregnancy to 19% in late-pregnancy, but background factors could not differentiate women with increasing or decreasing fear.
